newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: AFRICA USING LESS THAN SIX PCT OF HYDRO POTENTIAL.
newsitem.headline: AFRICA USING LESS THAN SIX PCT OF HYDRO POTENTIAL.

text.p: Less than six percent of Africa's hydro-electric power potential is being used, with the greatest untapped resources lying in the centre of the continent, an energy conference was told on Tuesday.
In a paper presented to the Africa Oil conference here, Bizuneh Fikru of the African Development Bank said Africa held 11.5 to 14.5 percent of the world's hydro-power potential.
But while North Afica was exploiting 30 percent of its limited resources and West Africa 13 percent, Central Africa was tapping just two percent.
In East Africa, useage averaged four percent and in Southern Africa three percent.

Lowest development costs were usually found in Central Africa with an average of $1,000 per kW in Zaire and Congo. Costs are estimated as low as $500 at the region's biggest prospect, the Inga site on the Zaire river.
Utilisation of this vast resource, however, is being held back by lack of integration of power networks within Africa, limiting the scope for exports from surplus to deficit areas.
